- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% relative to prior peak.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; cap forecast at +2% above prior peak.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show price decline, forecast should not drop below 1–2 standard deviations below recent low.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts; smooth forecast by averaging last 5–7 days’ values if sentiment volatility >0.4.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model tends to err on the side of overconfidence; apply a 1–2% downward adjustment to avoid overestimating upside.
